headline: Steroids kill neurons
body: and there are things that counter it

headline: The experiment
body: Cortical neurons grown from rat brain tissue. | Dosed with different androgens for 24 hours or 3 days. | They measured mitochondrial activity, *LDH release* which means membranes are leaking, and *caspase 3/7* which is the enzyme that executes apoptosis.
punch: Three separate readouts of cell death.

headline: Testosterone
body: nandrolone and trenbolone all killed neurons by **apoptosis**. | All three raised LDH release, so membranes were failing. | Caspase 3/7 went up, so the death was programmed rather than accidental.
punch: The cells were told to die. They did not just break.

headline: Stanozolol
body: killed them differently. | It caused *necrosis* instead of apoptosis and did not raise LDH the same way. | Necrosis is uncontrolled rupture, which triggers inflammation in the surrounding tissue.
punch: Not safer. A messier death with an inflammatory tail.

headline: Trenbolone
body: reduced **neurite outgrowth**. Neurites are the extensions neurons use to connect to each other. | It also downregulated *Tubb3*, the gene for beta 3 tubulin. | That is the structural protein neurons build those extensions from.
punch: It kills cells and stops the survivors wiring up.

headline: Nandrolone
body: hit mitochondria first. | Reduced mitochondrial activity by **24 hours**, before the apoptosis signal fired. | It reaches the failure point earlier than the others.
punch: Deca gets in sooner in the death pathway.

headline: The mechanism
body: They added *flutamide*, which blocks the androgen receptor. | The toxicity almost completely disappeared. Mitochondria kept working, membranes held, apoptosis was inhibited. | So the damage is **androgen receptor mediated**.
punch: The receptor doing the damage is the one you are using.

headline: Which tells you
body: You cannot block the receptor without losing the anabolic effect. | So mitigation has to work **downstream**, on the endpoints being damaged. | Those endpoints are named: apoptosis, mitochondrial function, neurite outgrowth, and neurotrophic factor expression.
punch: Target the damage, not the trigger.

headline: Cerebrolysin
body: is a peptide preparation containing fragments resembling *NGF*, *BDNF* and *ciliary neurotrophic factor*. | Clinically indicated for traumatic brain injury, stroke recovery and vascular dementia. | It promotes neurite outgrowth and neuronal survival, which are the exact things trenbolone suppresses.
punch: Cortexin is a related peptide preparation in the same class.

headline: 9-Me-BC
body: 9-methyl-beta-carboline inhibits *MAO* and stimulates **neurotrophic factor expression in astrocytes**. | It also raises *tyrosine hydroxylase* and dopaminergic transcription factors. | Astrocytes are the support cells that keep neurons alive.
punch: It raises the trophic support the neuron is losing.

headline: Memantine
body: is an NMDA receptor antagonist, approved for Alzheimer's. | It blocks excitotoxic calcium influx, which is a major upstream trigger of neuronal apoptosis. | *TAK-653* works the opposite direction as an AMPA positive modulator raising BDNF.
punch: Low dose ketamine raises BDNF through mTOR signalling.

headline: The honest part
body: **Nobody has tested any of these against AAS neurotoxicity directly.** That head to head study does not exist. | What exists is compounds that act on the specific endpoints this damage hits. | That is mechanistic reasoning, not a demonstrated result.

headline: And the base levers
body: still matter most. | Toxicity was **dose dependent**, and repeated exposure was worse than single dose. | Trenbolone hit neurite outgrowth and gene expression when others did not.
punch: Dose, duration and compound come before any peptide.
